recognize_zh: 拼圖中的中型淋巴母細胞核圓、染色質細緻呈顆粒狀，細胞質深藍色並含多個邊界清楚的透明脂質空泡，是 Burkitt 淋巴瘤的典型細胞學；但這是抹片而非組織切片，看不到標題描述的「星空」（starry sky）組織型態。
features: Composite of smear fields showing medium-sized, monomorphic lymphoid cells (about 2x a red cell)
Round to slightly squared nuclei with finely granular, stippled chromatin and small inconspicuous nucleoli
Scant to moderate deeply basophilic cytoplasm
Multiple sharply punched-out clear cytoplasmic (lipid) vacuoles, often also overlying the nucleus
Background of red cells without tingible body macrophages; histologic starry sky pattern not assessable
describe_en: Smear preparation (composite of several fields) shows medium-sized, monomorphic lymphoid cells with round nuclei, finely stippled chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli and scant deeply basophilic cytoplasm containing numerous sharply defined clear vacuoles. The cells occur singly and in small groups against a background of red cells; the specimen appears to be blood or a dilute aspirate. The starry sky pattern mentioned in the case description is a tissue-section finding and cannot be seen on this smear. The cytologic features are consistent with Burkitt lymphoma/leukemia, which requires confirmation by flow cytometry (CD10+, BCL6+, BCL2-, surface light chain restricted, Ki-67 near 100% on tissue) and demonstration of MYC rearrangement.

ddx.vs: Lymphoblasts have finer, more homogeneous chromatin, scant pale cytoplasm and few vacuoles, and are TdT/CD34 positive with no surface light chain, whereas Burkitt cells are TdT negative and surface immunoglobulin positive.

ddx.dx: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements
ddx.vs: Double-hit lymphoma can look Burkitt-like with vacuolated basophilic cytoplasm, but typically shows more nuclear pleomorphism, BCL2 protein expression and BCL2 rearrangement by FISH.

ddx.dx: Acute myeloid leukemia with vacuolated blasts (e.g., monoblastic)
ddx.vs: Vacuolated myeloid blasts have folded nuclei, prominent nucleoli, grey-blue cytoplasm and may show granules or Auer rods, and are MPO or nonspecific esterase positive rather than CD19/CD10 positive.
